clusters.name: foundation
clusters.executionModeRationale: Foundation cluster, runs alone in phase 1. Sets up the auth policy stub and review-required protocol so downstream stories can use them without re-touching.

clusters.name: envelope-and-identity
clusters.executionModeRationale: US-002 and US-006 are file-disjoint and both build foundation primitives required by US-003 and US-004. Can run in parallel inside phase 2; safe to run serially inside one implementer member.

clusters.name: member-tag-and-hooks

sharedFiles: hooks/mailbox.js (read-path: parseTurnTags, consumeMailbox manifest patch — distinct from envelope-and-identity's write-path edits)

clusters.executionModeRationale: Can run in parallel with envelope-and-identity because hooks/mailbox.js edits target different functions (parseTurnTags + consumeMailbox vs appendMailboxWithSender). Recommend SERIAL inside one impl member for safety; PARALLEL only if implementer is willing to handle a focused mailbox.js merge.

clusters.name: operator-cli

sharedFiles: hooks/commands/registry.js (3 new entries; also touched by escalate-slash)

clusters.executionModeRationale: Depends on envelope-and-identity. Shares registry.js with escalate-slash. Recommend SERIAL with escalate-slash to avoid a 4-entry merge conflict in registry.js, or accept the small conflict and resolve manually if running parallel.

clusters.name: escalate-slash
clusters.executionModeRationale: Same dependency surface as operator-cli. Could run in parallel with operator-cli inside phase 3 IF the implementer is comfortable resolving the registry.js merge. Recommend SERIAL after operator-cli for low-risk implementation.

clusters.name: integration-tail
clusters.executionModeRationale: Must run last because (a) visual prefixes need the new envelope kinds to exist, (b) cross-engine hook test needs US-005's stop-hook changes, (c) backwards-compat smoke needs the full v1.9.x writer surface, (d) docs reference all earlier-phase changes.
